newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF CEO says market trends confirm view.
newsitem.headline: SKF CEO says market trends confirm view.

text.p: Swedish roller bearing company SKF AB said on Monday market trends in the first two months of the year confirmed its view that markets outside Western Europe were showing positive development.

"We have begun the operational year at a low level in Western Europe while other markets continue to show a positive development for the company," SKF managing director Peter Augustsson said in the company's annual report.
He did not, however, expect the Western European market to weaken further.
Augustsson also said SKF would increase operations in Asia.
"Our investments in Asia are proceeding at a high tempo and we are continually strengthening our position on this important market," Augustsson said.
He said the company's result in 1996 was good but that he was not satisfied. SKF posted a profit of 2.41 billion crowns after financial items for 1996 compared to 3.39 billion in 1995.
"SKF has the potential for better profitability," he said.
